# 6. Layered Stack Detail

## 6.1 PHY / MAC

O-CPS is radio-agnostic within the constraints of regional regulation. Implementations MUST support at least one of: C-V2X PC5 (either LTE-V2X as specified in 3GPP Rel-14/16 or NR-V2X as specified in Rel-16 and later), or ITS-G5 as specified in IEEE 802.11p or its successor 802.11bd. Implementations intended for deployment in North America SHOULD prioritize C-V2X PC5 in Channel 183 (5.895–5.925 GHz) consistent with the FCC’s 2020 allocation. Implementations intended for deployment in the European Union SHOULD support both C-V2X and ITS-G5 on channels in the 5.875–5.905 GHz range per ETSI EN 302 571.

Dual-stack implementations MUST listen on all supported radios simultaneously and MUST NOT transmit duplicate application-layer messages across both radios without explicit congestion-control coordination; the decongestion algorithm specified in ETSI TS 103 175 applies.

## 6.2 Transport / Network

Over ITS-G5, O-CPS messages are carried in GeoNetworking packets with BTP-B (non-interactive) headers, per ETSI EN 302 636-4 and EN 302 636-5. Messages are addressed to a geographic destination area, typically a disc or rectangle centered on the transmitter and sized to the message’s relevance horizon (§9.1.4).

Over C-V2X PC5, messages are carried in sidelink bearers with ProSe Per-Packet Priority (PPPP) values assigned per message class (Table 9-2). NR-V2X implementations MAY use HARQ feedback as specified in 3GPP TS 38.321 for PerceptionSummary and Attestation messages; MUST NOT use HARQ for Intent messages, which have sub-100 ms deadlines that do not tolerate retransmission.

## 6.3 Security

Every O-CPS message that is transmitted over the air MUST be signed. The signature covers the entire message payload, including the timestamp field. Signatures are ECDSA over the NIST P-256 curve, computed over the SHA-256 hash of the payload. Signing keys are held in an HSM conformant to at least FIPS 140-3 Level 2 or Common Criteria EAL 4+.

Signing certificates are pseudonym certificates issued by a Security Credential Management System (SCMS) per IEEE 1609.2.1 or by a C-ITS PKI per ETSI TS 102 940 and TS 102 941. Pseudonym certificates have a maximum validity of one week and are rotated at a minimum interval specified in §10.1.2. Rotation uses butterfly key expansion per IEEE 1609.2.1 to provide unlinkability across certificate epochs.

## 6.4 Message

The message layer is specified in full in §9. It defines five message classes: PerceptionSummary, Intent, GroupState, Attestation, and Telemetry. All messages share a common header containing a timestamp, a pseudonym-certificate identifier, a message class identifier, and a sequence counter.

## 6.5 Perception and Fusion

The perception and fusion layer consumes incoming PerceptionSummary and Intent messages and fuses them with the vehicle’s local sensor output to produce a world model. Fusion is trust-weighted: the contribution of each source to a fused track depends on (a) the attestation state of the source, (b) the historical agreement between the source and local sensors, and (c) the self-reported confidence in the source message. The exact weighting function is implementation-defined, subject to the constraints in §12.

## 6.6 Application

The application layer hosts cooperative behaviors. This specification defines the C-ACC Group Protocol (§13.1) as a normative behavior. It defines Slipstream Mode (§13.2) and Intersection Assist (§13.3) as optional extensions. Other behaviors MAY be defined by extension profiles and MUST NOT conflict with the normative requirements of this document.
